Le subagent `ux-designer` a terminé. Voici son rapport verbatim : --- Not going to chase that further — this is a bounded fixture audit, not something requiring cross-session recall. Proceeding directly to the audit based on the file already read. ## Summary Audit of `tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/design_target.html` (33 lines, synthetic "Account Settings" form fixture) against WCAG 2.2 AA and Nielsen's 10 heuristics. Read-only audit — file not modified. ## User and task - **User segment:** Returning authenticated user, generalist competency, mixed input modality (keyboard, screen reader, touch/mobile) — the fixture makes no platform assumption, so all three must work. - **Task:** Correct an invalid email address in an account-settings form and save the change. - **Success criterion:** Field accepts a valid email, error state (if any) is announced to assistive tech and visible without color as the only cue, save action is reachable and operable by keyboard, ≤1 form re-submission needed. - **Failure modes:** user can't tell which field is labeled once they start typing; color-blind or screen-reader user can't perceive the error; keyboard-only user can't reach or activate Save; touch user mis-taps a target too small to hit; a close/dismiss control silently submits the form instead of dismissing. ## Stakes classification - **Classification: High** — this is a form on an "Account Settings" page (data-entry, account-modifying action), and per skill procedure Move 2, accessibility-critical forms are High stakes regardless of the surface's visual simplicity. Full Moves 1–6 discipline applies; the seven-step accessibility audit (Move 2 / §3 of the skill) is mandatory and every check must have a verified answer before this would be considered ready to ship. ## Violations found | # | Element (line) | Criterion | Severity | Minimal fix | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `` (line 13) | **WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A)** — also fails 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A), since the input has no programmatic name at all once the placeholder is treated as decorative | **Critical** | Add a persistent `` immediately before the input, and add `id="email"` to the input so the `for`/`id` pair associates them. Placeholder may stay as a supplementary hint but must not be the sole label. | | 2 | `Invalid format` (line 17) | **WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color (A)** — status conveyed by color alone, no icon/text word | **Critical** | Prepend a non-color cue, e.g. `⚠ Error: Invalid format` (icon/glyph + the word "Error" so the status survives grayscale/screen-reader rendering). | | 2b | Same span, line 17 (red `#FF0000` on unstated/default white background) | **WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA)** — computed contrast ratio of `#FF0000` on white is ≈4.0:1, below the 4.5:1 required for normal-size text | **Serious** | Darken the red to a WCAG-passing shade, e.g. `#B00020` (~5.9:1 on white), or increase to large-text size (≥18.66px bold / 24px) if the 3:1 large-text threshold is intentionally targeted instead. | | 2c | Same span, line 17 | **WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 Error Identification (A) / 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA)** — error text is not programmatically associated with the input (`aria-describedby`) and is not in a live region, so a screen-reader user editing the field is never told the error exists or which field it belongs to | **Serious** | Give the span an `id`, e.g. `id="email-error"`, add `aria-describedby="email-error"` to the input, and add `aria-live="polite"` (or `role="alert"`) to the span so the message is announced on appearance. | | 3 | `
Save changes
` (lines 22–24) | **WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (A)** and **SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)** — a `
` with only a click handler has no keyboard reachability, no `button` role, no built-in focus indicator | **Critical** | Replace with a native `` (drop the `onclick`, rely on native form submission or `onclick` on the button if JS-driven). Native element restores keyboard operability, role, and focus styling for free. | | 4 | `` (lines 28–30) | **WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA)** — 16×16 CSS px is under the 24×24 px AA floor | **Serious** | Increase to at least `width:24px; height:24px` (or remove the fixed sizing and let default button padding apply; 44×44 is the stricter AAA/mobile-canonical target if this is a touch surface). | | 4b | Same button, line 28 | **WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)** — `aria-label=""` is an empty string, which overrides the visible text content (`×`) and leaves the button with **no accessible name at all**; screen readers announce only "button" | **Critical** | Either delete the empty `aria-label=""` attribute (letting the `×` glyph serve as the accessible name — still weak) or, better, set `aria-label="Close"` (or "Dismiss") so the button has an actual accessible name matching its function. | | 5 | `
